courses.subject: YDSH
courses.title: Beginning Yiddish I
courses.description: Course develops basic conversational and reading skills as well as the essentials of Yiddish grammar.

courses.subject: YDSH
courses.title: Beginning Yiddish II
courses.description: Continuation of YDSH 101 focusing on comprehension and reading skills.

courses.subject: YDSH
courses.title: Intermediate Yiddish I
courses.description: Continuation of YDSH 102. Develops more advanced conversational, comprehension, reading and writing skills as well as introducing more advanced features of Yiddish grammar.

courses.subject: YDSH
courses.title: Intermediate Yiddish II
courses.description: Continuation of YDSH 203. Further development of advanced conversational, comprehension, grammar, and reading and writing skills.

courses.subject: YDSH
courses.title: Jewish Storytelling
courses.description: Course will introduce the great Jewish storytellers such as Nachman of Bratslav, Scholem-Aleichem, and I.B. Singer through readings of Yiddish tales, short stories, poetry, drama and excerpts from novels and autobiographies from the 19th and 20th centuries. In addition, Yiddish films and folklore will be used to exemplify the variety of Jewish cultural expression in Eastern Europe, Russia, and America. Course will also present a sample of critical approaches to Yiddish literature. Taught in English translation. Same as CWL 221, ENGL 223, JS 220, and REL 220.

courses.subject: YDSH
courses.title: Responses to the Holocaust
courses.description: Course introduces a variety of Jewish and non-Jewish responses to the Holocaust created during and after the Second World War (from 1939). The discussion of Holocaust films, miniseries, memoirs, diaries, novels, short stories, poems, and other texts will focus on the unique contribution of those works to our understanding of the Holocaust. In addition, the works and their authors will be situated in their cultural and historical context. Taught in English translation.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 320, ENGL 359, JS 320, and REL 320. See CWL 320.

courses.subject: YDSH
courses.title: Jewish Life-Writing
courses.description: Jewish life-writing from the late 18th century until today. Emphasis on cultural historical context, literary styles, and forms. All texts will be available in English translation. Same as CWL 421, HIST 436, REL 420, and SLAV 420. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
